questions.prompt: What specific morphological classification of sensory receptors is responsible for detecting noxious or tissue-damaging stimuli?
Identify the two primary categories of nociceptors based on the types of stimuli that activate them.
questions.modelAnswer: Thermal/mechanical nociceptors (activated by extremes of temperature/pressure) and polymodal nociceptors (activated by high-intensity mechanical, chemical, or thermal stimuli).

questions.prompt: Based on the Erlanger and Gasser classification, which myelinated nerve fibers are responsible for carrying "fast" (sharp, localized) pain?
Which unmyelinated, slow-conducting nerve fibers are responsible for transmitting "slow" (aching, burning, poorly localized) pain?
Name the two major excitatory neurotransmitters released by primary afferent nociceptors onto second-order neurons in the spinal cord.
According to the "gate-control" theory, how does the simultaneous stimulation of large-diameter A-beta mechanoreceptors alleviate the perception of pain?
questions.modelAnswer: Lateral inhibition: Stimulation of A-beta fibers activates inhibitory interneurons in the dorsal horn that "close the gate" to pain signals traveling through the smaller A-delta and C fibers.

questions.prompt: In the endogenous pain suppression system, how do opioids produce presynaptic inhibition of pain signals?
questions.modelAnswer: Opioids decrease calcium influx into the presynaptic terminal, which reduces the exocytosis of excitatory neurotransmitters (like Substance P).

questions.prompt: Describe the mechanism by which endogenous opioids produce postsynaptic inhibition on spinothalamic projection neurons.
questions.modelAnswer: Opioids increase potassium conductance, leading to potassium efflux and hyperpolarization of the postsynaptic neuron, making it less excitable.

questions.prompt: Explain the "convergence-projection theory" as the physiological basis for referred pain.
questions.modelAnswer: Visceral nociceptive fibers and somatic fibers from the skin converge on the same second-order neurons in the dorsal horn; the brain "projects" the sensation to the skin rather than the internal organ.

questions.prompt: Which specific region of the midbrain is a critical component of the descending pain suppression system, relaying signals to the nucleus raphe magnus?
Define "hyperalgesia" and identify the role of prostaglandins in this process.
questions.modelAnswer: Hyperalgesia is an increased sensitivity or reduced threshold for pain following tissue injury; prostaglandins sensitize the nociceptors but do not directly excite them.

questions.prompt: Why is visceral pain frequently associated with autonomic responses such as nausea, sweating, and changes in blood pressure?
questions.modelAnswer: Visceral pain is carried primarily by C fibers that have sparse innervation and travel via sympathetic and parasympathetic nerves, allowing signals to reach brain stem centers that coordinate autonomic reflexes.
